phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-dining-room
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-dining-room
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-hallway
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-hallway
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-hallway
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-hallway
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.

phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-living-room
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

SWITCH:on)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bedroom
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bedroom
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bedroom
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bedroom
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-office
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-office
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bathroom
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bathroom
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)

phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:

SWITCH:off

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)

phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness

[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-outdoor
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-outdoor
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bathroom
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bathroom
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: State-Update Delay Attack (Fu et al. Type 1)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay device state-change events via transparent TCP proxy while maintaining keepalives to avoid offline alerts. Demonstrated 5.0s delay on IoT event messages.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Critical state updates (intrusion, smoke, water leak) delayed by 5.0s. Hub's world-model is stale. Real-time alerting value destroyed. Fu et al. demonstrated up to 40 minutes on HomeKit, 64s on Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Application-layer event acknowledgment with timestamps, accessory keepalive mechanism, event freshness validation, end-to-end encryption with replay protection
evidence:
Initial device state: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bedroom
SWITCH:off
BRIGHTNESS:100
Triggered state change: ON at t=0.000s
[Proxy] TCP connection maintained — device sees ACK (no offline alert)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Erroneous Automation Execution (Fu et al. Type 2)
phantom_delay_results.description: Delay trigger event so automation evaluates with stale state, causing incorrect execution. Exploits lack of event timestamp validation in IoT platforms.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Automations execute with wrong world-model state. Safety-critical automations (door locks, alarms, gas shutoff) can be triggered incorrectly or prevented. Fu et al. demonstrated on both Apple HomeKit and Ring.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Include monotonic timestamps in event messages, validate event freshness before automation evaluation, application-layer event acknowledgment (HAP Section 6.8.2)
evidence: [Setup] Automation rule: IF motion_detected AND is_dark THEN light.ON

[t=0.0s] Motion sensor fires trigger event (response: VESPER-FW generic vesper-3d-bedroom
SWITCH:on)
→ Automation should NOT fire (condition no longer met)

phantom_delay_results.attack_name: Action Reorder Attack (Fu et al. Type 4)
phantom_delay_results.description: Reorder commands by selectively delaying the first, causing it to override the second. Device ends in attacker-desired state instead of user-intended state.
phantom_delay_results.impact: Device commands arrive out of order. Earlier (attacker-desired) command overrides later (user-intended) command. Security system left disarmed, locks left unlocked.
phantom_delay_results.mitigation: Implement command sequence numbers, reject out-of-order commands, use vector clocks or Lamport timestamps, validate command freshness
evidence: [t=0.0s] Cloud sends DISARM (OFF) command → attacker delays for 5.0s
[t=0.5s] User manually ARMs (ON) system → delivered immediately

network_attacks_results.mitigation: Use Docker macvlan networks, enable ARP inspection, static ARP entries
evidence: ARP cache poisoning would redirect gateway traffic through attacker
Docker bridge networks are vulnerable to ARP spoofing by default
Requires --mac-address control and raw socket access

network_attacks_results.description: Poison DNS to redirect device cloud connections to attacker
network_attacks_results.impact: Credential theft, malicious firmware delivery, data exfiltration
network_attacks_results.mitigation: Use DNSSEC, certificate pinning, encrypted DNS (DoH/DoT)
evidence: IoT devices rarely validate DNS responses (no DNSSEC)

network_attacks_results.description: Send deauthentication frames to disconnect WiFi IoT devices
network_attacks_results.impact: Device offline, DoS, force reconnection to evil twin
network_attacks_results.mitigation: WPA3 with Protected Management Frames (PMF)
evidence: Reason code: 7 (Class 3 frame from non-associated station)
